title: Consumer IR remote receiver: NEC and RC-5 decode, codes to a ring in memory over AXI4
features: ir_in is the demodulated receiver output, active low. A tick is TICK_DIV + 1 clocks: NEC unit = 16 ticks (562.5 us at a 35.16 us tick), RC-5 half bit = 25 ticks (889 us); pulse widths are accepted within +-25%.
MODE 0 NEC (address, inverted address or extended address, command, inverted command, repeat codes), MODE 1 RC-5 (toggle, 5-bit address, 6-bit command with field bit).
Each code is one ring word {proto[1:0], repeat, toggle, 4'b0, addr_hi, addr, cmd}; LAST shows the newest code.
Ring of RING_WORDS words at RING_BASE (WR_IDX / RD_IDX); 8 codes wait in a FIFO while the ring is full, then OVF_CNT counts the lost ones.

fields.desc: codes lost to a full ring and FIFO

irqs.name: ERR
irqs.desc: a job ended that saw an AXI error response

sequence: Write TICK_DIV (clock / 28.44 kHz - 1), RING_BASE, RING_WORDS, RD_IDX = 0.
Write CTRL (enable, mode) and IRQ_ENABLE with CODE.
On CODE, read LAST or the ring words RD_IDX .. WR_IDX - 1 and write RD_IDX.
notes: m_* is the AXI4 manager port (32-bit address and data, 4-bit ID, no user / QoS); it passes through unchanged. Bursts are INCR, AxSIZE = 2 (4 bytes), 1 to 16 beats, WSTRB = 4'hF, never across a 4 KB boundary; one read and one write burst are outstanding at a time.
ir_in is the receiver pin (idle high).
The core testbench prints one `LAT <master> dram R|W <cycles>` line per AXI burst (tb/tv_lat_mon.svh), the regression suite's latency format.
